sources.note: ERS's own programme page for the VISIT grant (page banner reads 'CALL OPEN'). Confirms awarding body, programme purpose, duration, and the 2026 cycle dates.

ERS fellowship portfolio page. Its comparison table has a VISIT row (duration up to 1 month; applicants profile 'PhD, MD(Resp), or equivalent'; mobility 'Any institute in Europe or abroad'; next deadline 31 October 2026; status Open).

'VISIT Grant Application Guidance 2026' PDF, linked as a document on the ERS VISIT page. The shared-link page itself requires JavaScript, so the PDF bytes were read from ERS's Box download endpoint https://ers.box.com/index.php?rm=box_download_shared_file&shared_name=hxefcfvjafjk0qfe86k4f8u9ntxupzgl&file_id=f_2274197394431 (8 pages, dated 09.06.2026/V1).
ERS VISIT Grant application form 2026 (.docx, linked from the ERS VISIT page). Confirms the submission route and the signed eligibility declarations.

awarding_body.detail: The page is the European Respiratory Society's own site (ersnet.org) and names ERS as the awarding body. ERS's Swiss base also matches the record's country: the guidance carries the letterhead 'ERS Headquarters, 4 Avenue Ste-Luce, CH1003 Switzerland'. Not an aggregator, news article or blog.
awarding_body.quote: European Respiratory Society (ERS) Visiting Mid-Career Investigator Travel (VISIT) Grants offer mid-career investigators, clinicians and allied healthcare professionals who are transitioning to more established stages of their careers to visit an institution(s) outside of their home country for up to one month.

deadline.detail: The page publishes 31 October 2026 as the application deadline and the cycle is open today (12 October 2026): the banner reads 'CALL OPEN', the call opened 13 July 2026, and the portfolio table lists status 'Open' with next deadline '31 October, 2026'. The guidance adds the exact cut-off time. This matches the record's deadline_date 2026-10-31.
deadline.quote: Application deadline: 31 October, 2026 — and in the guidance: 'The deadline for submitting applications is 31 October 2026 at 23:59 pm CET.'

eligibility.detail: Confirmed: the target group is 'mid-career investigators, clinicians and allied healthcare professionals'; visits must be outside the applicant's home country for one week up to one month; there is no nationality restriction ('All nationalities, European and non-European based applicants may submit a proposal'); and the host country rule matches the record ('exchanges between two institutions within the same country are not allowed'). Not confirmed: the record states that all three groups must hold 'a PhD, an MD in respiratory medicine or an equivalent qualification', but the guidance sets a lower bar for one of the three named groups - allied healthcare professionals need only an MSc. Two material requirements are also missing from the record's summary: at least one year of ERS active membership, and the mid-career career-stage rule (within 5 years of appointment to Associate Professor/Reader level, professor title holders ineligible).
eligibility.quote: Clinicians and researchers must hold a postgraduate degree such as PhD, MD(Res) or equivalent. / Allied healthcare professionals must hold a minimum of an MSc, or equivalent degree at the time of the application. / Applicants must be ERS active members for at least one year when applying for the ERS Mid-Career Investigator travel grant. / The application for ERS VISIT grant is open to those within 5 years of appointment to clinical or academic equivalent of Associate Professor / Reader level (taking into consideration any work hiatus period which will be deducted). / Applicants holding a professor title are not eligible to apply.

funding.detail: The record's 'Partially Funded' is correct. The award is a fixed travel grant plus a per-diem only: EUR 600 for mobility between European countries, EUR 2,000 for long-distance Europe/non-Europe mobility, and EUR 200 per day for accommodation and meals. It covers no tuition, no stipend/salary and no other costs, and the guidance explicitly says undergraduate study is out of scope. This is a partial award, not a fully funded one.
funding.quote: Travel allowance €600 for mobility between European countries (including both EU and non-EU states) / €2'000 for mobility from Europe to non-Europe, or non-Europe to Europe (long distance flight) / Accommodation / meals allowance €200 (fixed amount per day of stay and travel) / No additional costs will be considered.

degree_levels.detail: The programme is a short-term travel/mobility grant, not a degree programme, so no degree level is offered or implied; the page says it 'is not for clinical training or research projects' and the guidance that it 'does not cover undergraduate studies'. The only study-level statement is the applicant profile in ERS's own portfolio table ('PhD, MD(Resp), or equivalent') plus the mid-career career-stage rule, which points at established rather than postdoctoral-stage applicants. The record's 'Postdoctoral' label is therefore not supported by the pages read.
degree_levels.quote: This programme is not for clinical training or research projects. / ERS VISIT programme is not meant to exchange expertise regarding teaching or science and, therefore, does not cover undergraduate studies and is not designed solely to cover the costs of attending workshops, courses, conferences or congresses.

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Application deadline: 31 October, 2026 (guidance: 'The deadline for submitting applications is 31 October 2026 at 23:59 pm CET.')
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Official ERS page and the linked ERS VISIT Grant Application Guidance 2026 (09.06.2026/V1, Box) both read on 2026-10-12. Deadline and awarding body verified: 2026 cycle is open (call opened 13 July 2026, deadline 31 October 2026 23:59 CET, decisions mid-February 2027, visits may start 1 March 2027 and must finish within 12 months). Two claims could not be confirmed and need a human decision before the record can go active: (1) degree_levels 'Postdoctoral' - this is a travel/mobility grant, not a degree programme, and eligible applicants are mid-career (within 5 years of Associate Professor/Reader appointment; professor title holders ineligible); (2) eligibility_summary - the PhD/MD requirement applies only to clinicians and researchers; allied healthcare professionals need only an MSc, and two requirements are missing entirely: ERS active membership for at least one year, and the 5-years-from-Associate-Professor career-stage rule. Funding confirmed partial: EUR 600 travel (Europe-Europe) or EUR 2,000 (long distance) plus EUR 200/day accommodation-meals, no tuition or stipend. Applications go to scientific@ersnet.org, not via an online portal.

notes_for_reviewer: Two edits need a human decision, which is why this is needs_review rather than active. First, degree_levels says 'Postdoctoral': ERS's own portfolio table describes the VISIT applicant profile as 'PhD, MD(Resp), or equivalent' with duration 'Up to 1' month, and the guidance requires applicants to be within 5 years of appointment to Associate Professor/Reader level while barring anyone holding a professor title - i.e. mid-career, not postdoctoral, and not a degree course at all. Second, the eligibility_summary over-generalises the degree requirement and omits two hard requirements: at least one year of ERS active membership, and the career-stage window. Everything else (body, deadline for the currently-open cycle, partial funding) checked out cleanly against the official page and the official guidance PDF, so only those two fields should change if the reviewer accepts the rewording.
